[[File:Columbus-ohio-nationwide-arena.jpg|thumb|The Blue Jackets have played their home games at the [[Nationwide Arena]] since their inaugural season.]]
The [[Columbus Blue Jackets]] are an American professional [[ice hockey]] team based in [[Columbus, Ohio]]. They play in the [[Metropolitan Division]] of the [[Eastern Conference (NHL)|Eastern Conference]] in the [[National Hockey League]] (NHL).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nhl.com/ice/teams.htm|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090311030113/http://www.nhl.com/ice/teams.htm|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 11, 2009|title=Teams|publisher=Lincoln Hockey and the National Hockey League|work=NHL.com|accessdate=January 5, 2009}}</ref> The team joined the NHL in 2000 as an [[expansion team]]. The Blue Jackets have played their home games at the [[Nationwide Arena]] since their inaugural season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://bluejackets.nhl.com/team/app?service=page&page=NHLPage&bcid=new_his_timeline#2000 |title=Blue Jackets Franchise Timeline |publisher=Lincoln Hockey and the National Hockey League |accessdate=January 5, 2009 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20070710205758/http://bluejackets.nhl.com/team/app?service=page&page=NHLPage&bcid=new_his_timeline |archivedate=July 10, 2007}}</ref> The franchise is owned by John P. McConnell and [[Don Waddell]] is their [[general manager]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://bluejackets.nhl.com/team/FrontOfficeStaff.htm|title=Front Office Staff Directory|publisher=Lincoln Hockey and the National Hockey League|accessdate=January 5, 2009|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20090118225019/http://bluejackets.nhl.com/team/FrontOfficeStaff.htm|archivedate=January 18, 2009}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://bluejackets.nhl.com/team/app?service=page&page=TeamPlayers&type=roster |title=Players |publisher=Lincoln Hockey and the National Hockey League |accessdate=January 5, 2009 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20090301060640/http://bluejackets.nhl.com/team/app?service=page&page=TeamPlayers&type=roster |archivedate=March 1, 2009}}</ref>

There have been 12 full-time [[head coach]]es for the Blue Jackets franchise. The team's first head coach was [[Dave King (ice hockey)|Dave King]], who coached for three seasons. [[Ken Hitchcock]] coached the team to its first playoff appearance. [[Scott Arniel]] was the head coach of the Blue Jackets from 2010 through 2012.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hockey-reference.com/teams/CBJ/coaches.html|title=Columbus Blue Jackets Coach Register|publisher=Sports Reference LLC|work=Hockey-Reference.com|accessdate=July 2, 2010}}</ref> [[Todd Richards (ice hockey)|Todd Richards]] was named interim head coach on January 9, 2012, and would remain with the team for more than 3½ seasons.<ref>{{cite web |title=Jackets dismiss Arniel; name Richards coach |url=http://www.nhl.com/ice/news.htm?id=610669 |website=NHL.com |access-date=December 23, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120112045332/http://www.nhl.com/ice/news.htm?id=610669 |archive-date=January 12, 2012 |date=January 9, 2012}}</ref> [[John Tortorella]] became the head coach on October 21, 2015, and left the team following the [[2020–21 NHL season|2020–21 season]] with the Blue Jackets' highest [[winning percentage]] (.568).<ref>{{cite web |title=CBJ, John Tortorella mutually agree to part ways |url=https://www.nhl.com/bluejackets/news/cbj-john-tortorella-mutually-agree-to-part-ways-324525908 |website=NHL.com |access-date=December 23, 2024 |date=May 9, 2021}}</ref> Tortorella was replaced by [[Brad Larsen]],<ref>{{cite web |title=CBJ name Brad Larsen head coach |url=https://www.nhl.com/bluejackets/news/cbj-name-brad-larsen-head-coach-325291980 |website=NHL.com |access-date=June 11, 2021 |date=June 10, 2021}}</ref> who served as head coach for two years before being fired at the conclusion of the {{nhly|2022}} season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Columbus Blue Jackets relieve Brad Larsen of his duties as head coach|url=https://www.nhl.com/bluejackets/news/columbus-blue-jackets-relieve-brad-larsen-of-his-duties-as-head-coach-343568366|publisher=NHL Enterprises, L. P.|website=NHL.com|access-date=April 15, 2023|date=April 15, 2023}}</ref> [[Mike Babcock]] was subsequently hired to replace Larsen;<ref>{{cite web |title=Columbus Blue Jackets name Mike Babcock ninth head coach in club history |url=https://www.nhl.com/bluejackets/news/columbus-blue-jackets-name-mike-babcock-ninth-head-coach-in-club-histo-345154864 |website=NHL.com |access-date=July 5, 2023 |date=July 1, 2023}}</ref> however, Babcock resigned before coaching a game for Columbus, after allegations of improper behavior via the ''[[Spittin' Chiclets]]'' podcast led to an [[National Hockey League Players' Association|NHLPA]] investigation.<ref name="BabcockVincent">{{cite web |url=https://www.nhl.com/bluejackets/news/mike-babcock-resigns-blue-jackets-name-pascal-vincent-head-coach |title=Mike Babcock resigns as head coach of the Columbus Blue Jackets; Club names Pascal Vincent head coach |website=NHL.com |date=September 17, 2023 |access-date=September 17, 2023}}</ref> After Babcock's resignation, [[Pascal Vincent]] was subsequently named head coach.<ref name="BabcockVincent" /> Vincent was subsequently fired after just one season as head coach, later being replaced by [[Dean Evason]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nhl.com/news/dean-evason-hired-as-columbus-blue-jackets-coach |title=Evason hired as Blue Jackets coach, replaces Vincent |website=NHL.com |date=July 22, 2024 |access-date=July 22, 2024}}</ref> Following just a season and a half as head coach, Evason himself was fired, being replaced by [[Rick Bowness]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nhl.com/news/columbus-fires-dean-evason-names-rick-bowness-new-head-coach |title=Evason fired as Blue Jackets coach, replaced by Bowness |website=NHL.com |date=January 12, 2026 |access-date=January 12, 2026}}</ref>
